title: LIVE UPDATES: Marcos in China for 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting
summary: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. went to China on Thursday to attend the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting a day after wrapping up Manila's chairmanship and hosting of the ASEAN Summit.

blocks.text: Published November 19, 2026 12:59am

APEC leaders and their spouses gather with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Madame Peng Liyuan for the official group photo at the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China. President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. and First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos join their fellow leaders and spouses for the occasion. (Photo from Presidential Communications Office)
Xi Jinping gives Marcos, FL Liza official welcome

SHENZHEN — President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. and First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos were given an official welcome by Chinese President Xi Jinping and First Lady Peng Liyuan on Wednesday evening in this city for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting.
Marcos and First Lady Liza joined their fellow leaders and spouses tonight for a gala dinner and cultural presentation.
The event was meant for “cultural celebration, friendship, and camaraderie,” bringing together leaders and their spouses at the APEC summit,” according to the Presidential Communications Office.
Marcos and his entire delegation arrived in China at 5:30 p.m. today.
The APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held from November 18 to 19, preceded by an annual summit of CEOs on November 17 to 18.

On Thursday, Marcos is expected to have bilateral meetings with three world leaders: Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast, Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori, and Papua New Guinea Prime Minister James Marape.
Marcos' visit in China comes after the Philippines' hosting of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit and Related Summits from November 15 to 17, 2026.
APEC is a regional forum of 21 member economies in the Asia-Pacific. The theme of this year's summit is "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together."

Marcos arrives in China to attend APEC Leaders' Meeting
SHENZHEN, China — President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. arrived in China on Wednesday ahead of his participation in the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting.
The PR001 carrying the President and his delegation landed at the Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport at 5:30 p.m.
Marcos is expected to attend a gala dinner in Shenzhen tonight (Wednesday evening).

According to Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro, Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, Cabinet Secretary Benhur Abalos, and Agrarian Reform Secretary Conrado Estrella III will serve as the country’s caretakers while Marcos is in China from November 18 to 20.
Xi, Putin blast Western 'protectionism,' sanctions before meeting Trump at APEC

SHENZHEN, China — China's President Xi Jinping on Wednesday pledged to stand up against trade protectionism, while his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin criticized Western sanctions as the two set the stage for a high-stakes trilateral meeting with Donald Trump.

They delivered their speeches at an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen, ahead of US President Trump's arrival from Manila, where he was meeting key regional allies.

The three men are due to meet on the sidelines on Thursday and potentially discuss Russia's war with Ukraine and the US war in Iran, as well as other flashpoints such as trade, AI and nuclear weapons.

The meeting has drawn comparisons with the 1945 Yalta Conference between the US, Britain and the Soviet Union that formalized spheres of influence, set the stage for the post-World War Two order and became shorthand for great-power deals imposed on smaller countries.
China's Xi calls for free and open trade at APEC CEO Summit

SHENZHEN, China - Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday urged support for "free and open trade," while expressing opposition to "protectionism" in an opening speech at an Asia-Pacific summit where he was due to meet his US and Russian counterparts.

Xi's remarks came after Washington announced further restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips from companies such as Nvidia, which could further complicate a fragile trade truce with Beijing. China has pledged to retaliate.

"We must firmly uphold the rules-based multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core, support free and open trade and investment, maintain the stability and smooth operation of global industrial and supply chains," Xi told an audience of business executives, after posing a series of rhetorical questions on how the Asia Pacific should respond to a changing world.
Western trade partners have criticized China for running annual trade surpluses in excess of $1 trillion through policies that support its manufacturing sector at the expense of its consumers.
Marcos flies to China for APEC Summit
President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Wednesday afternoon left Manila to participate in the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen, China.
The PR001 carrying the President and his delegation left Villamor Air Base at 3:25 p.m.

With Marcos are First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, Finance Secretary Frederick Go, Trade and Industry Secretary Cristina Roque, Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro, and Presidential Communications Office Secretary Lino Cayetano.
They are expected to land at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport past 5 p.m.
